pr_title: roachtest: initialize system before restricting lease transfers
pr_body:
The test would previously set the parameter
`COCKROACH_DISABLE_LEADER_FOLLOWS_LEASEHOLDER` prior to initializing the
kv workload wth 1K splits. This would occasionally fail due to
rebalancing of ranges post-split. This commit allows all the splits and
rebalances to happen prior to setting this flat.

Epic: none
Fixes: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/111068
Fixes: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/110842

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/112123)
PS: thoughts on why this started flaking so much now?

> PS: thoughts on why this started flaking so much now?

I don't exactly know why it is flaking so much more, and I was unable to reproduce it with 50 runs (I tried running with --count 10 - 5 times and 100% passed.) From what I could track in the failures, there was typically one range which got into an "atomic configuration" and then lost the lease in that configuration. Typically the allocator won't cause this by itself, but a combination of the store rebalancer and the allocator running at the same time can cause this to happen. We have made a number of changes to the store rebalancer over the past 2-3 months, so maybe it is a little more sensitive to this workload. I will look through the failure logs one more time to try and figure it out.

bors r+

I'm going to merge this so that we can figure out the problem later with nightlies. I can't run roachtests this morning and initial testing seems to show that we don't ever do anything in those relocate lines (nothing escaped constraints for me). If anything we should track down why things were previously escaping constraints and fix them.
Yeah, the escaped constraints only happened once in a while. Let's leave it to the nightlies to figure out.

Its likely due to COCKROACH_DISABLE_LEADER_FOLLOWS_LEASEHOLDER since the replicate queue (which is what ALTER RANGE RELOCATE ends up calling) will not move things if the leader and leaseholder are not colocated. Changing this is somewhat invasive, as there are a few different checks that happen in this code path. I'm going to try instead to change it to move all the replicas, then restart the process after ranges are colocated.
